Types

Toilet suites: back to wall, close coupled and wall faced

Toilet suites are sold as a pan, a cistern and usually a seat. A back to wall toilet suite is a common choice in a renovation, because it hides the pipework and is simple to clean around.

How do the toilet suite types compare?

TypeWhat it isCleaningPlumbing
Back to wall toilet suiteThe pan and cistern sit flush against the wall, with no gap behindEasy: no pipes or gaps showingS trap or P trap, with the set-out checked against the pan
Close coupled suiteThe cistern sits on the back of the pan, and the pan stands clear of the wallMore surfaces and a gap behind the panThe most forgiving for an existing set-out
Wall faced pan with in-wall cisternThe pan sits against the wall and the cistern is hidden inside itEasy, with only the flush plate on showThe cistern is built into the wall frame before tiling
Wall hung pan with in-wall cisternThe pan hangs off a frame in the wall, clear of the floorThe floor underneath can be moppedNeeds a frame and a wall designed for it

A general comparison. Your plumber confirms what suits your bathroom.

A wall faced toilet suite pairs a floor pan with an in-wall cistern, and the range includes Geberit and R&T cisterns with a choice of flush plates.

Pricing

Toilet suite prices

7 toilet suites show their price on this site, from $280 to $400: Cleanman, Livis, Mira, Qubist, Theo, Vivid and Ovo Toilet. Each is a complete suite.

The rest of the range shows Enquire Now. In-wall suites are priced as a combination of pan, cistern and flush plate, so the team confirms the price for the combination you choose.

Rimless

Rimless pans and why they are easier to clean

A traditional pan has a hollow rim that water flows through, and the underside of that rim is hard to reach with a brush. A rimless toilet has an open bowl with no hidden channel, so the whole surface can be wiped.

35 products on this page are described as rimless, and 24 use a tornado flush, which sends water around the bowl in a spiral.

Measuring

Set-out, S trap and P trap: what to measure

An S trap sends the waste down through the floor. A P trap sends it back through the wall. The set-out is the distance from the finished wall to the centre of the waste pipe.

Each suite lists the set-out range it suits. The Livis, for example, is supplied with a trap for a 100 to 170 mm set-out, with other traps as options. Measure yours before you choose, or ask your plumber for the figure.

Availability

Toilet availability and order times

Send the product name or code and your set-out, and the team confirms what can be supplied and when. For an in-wall suite, the cistern is needed first, before the wall is sheeted and tiled.

Choosing

Picking a toilet for your plumbing

If the waste is staying where it is, the set-out and trap type narrow the choice first. Then choose the pan height, the flush type and the seat.

If the room is being re-plumbed, you have a free choice, including a wall hung pan. Decide early, because it changes the wall frame. Choose the toilet alongside the vanity range so the two sit comfortably side by side.

Warranty

Warranty on pans, cisterns and seats

Pans, cisterns, seats and in-wall cisterns can each carry a different maker's warranty period. Ceramic is usually covered for longer than seats and cistern fittings, which are wearing parts.

Ask us for the warranty terms of the suite you choose. A warranty depends on installation by a licensed plumber.

Delivery

Delivery in Sydney

We deliver across Sydney metro. A toilet suite is boxed as a pan and a cistern, and a boxed pan weighs around 40 kg, so it is a two person lift.

Toilets are one part of the range. See everything for the bathroom and put the whole list on one enquiry.

The range

Poseidon toilet suites

The suites come from Poseidon's KDK and VITO ranges, with series including Avis, Avery, Qubist, Zeus, Stella, Elvera and Veda. Colours include gloss white, matte white and black.

The range also covers smart toilets and bidets, an accessible care range with grab rails, and the fittings a plumber needs: inlet and outlet valves, traps and fixings.

Seats

Toilet seat care and replacement seats

Clean the seat with a soft cloth and mild detergent. Bleach and abrasive cleaners damage the surface and the hinges.

38 replacement seats and seat fittings are listed on this page, each named with the pans it suits. Match the seat code to your pan, and finish the room with matching accessories.

Toilets

Toilet questions

What is a rimless toilet?

A rimless toilet has a pan with no hollow rim around the top. Water is directed around the open bowl instead, which leaves no hidden channel for dirt and makes the pan easier to clean.

How do I measure a toilet set-out?

For an S trap, measure from the finished wall to the centre of the waste pipe in the floor. For a P trap, measure from the finished floor to the centre of the pipe in the wall. Give that figure to us or your plumber.

What is the difference between back to wall and close coupled?

A back to wall suite sits flush against the wall with no gap behind the pan. A close coupled suite has the cistern mounted on the pan, and the pan stands clear of the wall.

How much is a toilet suite?

The toilet suites with a price on this site run from $280 to $400. In-wall and other suites show Enquire Now and are priced when you enquire.

Do toilet suites come with the seat?

Many do. Livis, Qubist and Theo list a seat as supplied. Check the description of the suite you choose, as some pans are sold without a seat.

What WELS rating do your toilets have?

The Ovo Toilet is listed with a 4 star WELS rating and a 3.4 litre average flush. Most other suites list a 4.5 and 3 litre dual flush, and their star rating is not shown on this site, so ask us for the rating of the model you choose.
